chapter.title: Subject-Verb Agreement
chapter.description: Learn the core rules governing how singular and plural subjects agree with their corresponding verbs, including compound subjects, indefinite pronouns, collective nouns, and special phrases.

rules.title: Basic Singular and Plural Agreement
rules.explanation: A singular subject takes a singular verb, while a plural subject takes a plural verb.
rules.example: The dog barks. / The dogs bark.

rules.title: Compound Subjects with 'And'
rules.explanation: Two or more subjects joined by 'and' usually take a plural verb.
rules.example: Emily and Greg come to my house every Friday.

rules.title: Subjects Joined by 'Or' / 'Nor' (or 'Either...or' / 'Neither...nor')
rules.explanation: When two subjects are joined by 'or' or 'nor', the verb agrees with the subject closest to it.
rules.example: Either my mother or my father is coming. / Neither my friends nor I am interested.

rules.title: Intervening Phrases and Parenthetical Expressions
rules.explanation: Words or phrases coming between the subject and the verb (e.g., 'together with', 'along with', 'as well as', 'including') do not change the number of the subject.
rules.example: The Prime Minister, together with his wife, greets the press.

rules.title: Indefinite Pronouns
rules.explanation: Pronouns like 'everyone', 'everybody', 'someone', 'nobody', 'each', and 'one' are grammatically singular. Pronouns like 'few', 'many', and 'several' are plural.
rules.example: Everyone needs time to relax. / A few think it is too complicated.

rules.title: Plural-Form Nouns and Collective Nouns
rules.explanation: Nouns representing pairs (e.g., 'pants', 'tweezers', 'trousers') take plural verbs. Collective nouns (e.g., 'jury', 'committee', 'team') usually take singular verbs when acting as a single unit.
rules.example: Your pants are at the cleaner's. / The jury was not convinced.

questions.question: His pants ____ torn during the match.
questions.explanation: Nouns that exist as pairs or plural forms (like 'pants') take a plural verb. Since the event occurred in the past, 'were' is correct.

questions.question: Aron, together with his wife ____ the guests of the party.
questions.explanation: Phrases like 'together with' do not make the subject plural. The verb agrees with 'Aron' (singular).

questions.question: Tweezers ____ always useful to handle small objects.
questions.explanation: 'Tweezers' is a plural noun and requires a plural verb.

questions.question: The jury ____ not convinced.
questions.explanation: 'Jury' is a collective noun acting as a single unit, requiring a singular verb.

questions.question: The truthful ____ always trustworthy.
questions.explanation: Adjectives preceded by 'the' acting as plural subject nouns take a plural verb.

questions.question: To cry ____ never the solution to any problems.
questions.explanation: An infinitive phrase acting as a subject takes a singular verb.

questions.question: A number of soldiers ____ injured during the war.
questions.explanation: 'A number of' takes a plural verb, whereas 'The number of' takes a singular verb.

questions.question: The number of deceased soldiers ____ not stored in the record book.
questions.explanation: 'The number of' specifies a single total count and requires a singular verb.

questions.question: Killing ____ not always considered a bad thing.
questions.explanation: A gerund used as a subject takes a singular verb.

questions.question: There ____ many difficulties regarding the situation.
questions.explanation: In sentences starting with 'There', the verb agrees with the subject following it ('difficulties').

questions.question: Emily and Greg ( comes, come ) to my house every Friday for lunch.
questions.explanation: Compound subjects joined by 'and' take a plural verb.

questions.question: There ( is, are ) time to watch the movie.
questions.explanation: The subject 'time' is singular, so it takes 'is'.

questions.question: My friends who are in the band ( wants, want ) me to play a musical instrument.
questions.explanation: The main subject 'friends' is plural, so it requires 'want'.

questions.question: My father or my brothers ( is, are ) coming with me to the ball game.
questions.explanation: With subjects connected by 'or', the verb agrees with the closer subject ('brothers').

questions.question: Everyone ( needs, need ) time to relax.
questions.explanation: 'Everyone' is an indefinite pronoun and takes a singular verb.

questions.question: That bag of oranges ( looks, look ) fresh.
questions.explanation: The subject is 'bag' (singular), not 'oranges'.

questions.question: The lacrosse team ( hopes, hope ) to win the tournament next week.
questions.explanation: 'Team' is a collective noun functioning as a single unit.

questions.question: Your trousers ( needs, need ) to be cleaned.
questions.explanation: 'Trousers' is a plural noun.

questions.question: Some of the books on the shelf ( is, are ) dusty.
questions.explanation: 'Some' refers to 'books' (plural), requiring 'are'.

questions.question: Even though the students like the class, a few ( thinks, think ) that it is too complicated.
questions.explanation: 'A few' refers to plural items/people and takes a plural verb.

questions.question: Choose the sentence in which the subject and verb agree.
options: Every one of the shirts has a green collar.
Every one of the shirts have a green collar.
questions.answer: Every one of the shirts has a green collar.
questions.explanation: The singular subject 'Every one' takes the singular verb 'has'.

questions.question: Choose the sentence in which the subject and verb agree.
options: This singer, along with a few others, play the harmonica on stage.
This singer, along with a few others, plays the harmonica on stage.
questions.answer: This singer, along with a few others, plays the harmonica on stage.
questions.explanation: The phrase 'along with a few others' does not alter the singular subject 'singer'.

questions.question: Choose the sentence in which the subject and verb agree.
options: Sandals and towels are essential gear for a trip to the beach.
Sandals and towels is essential gear for a trip to the beach.
questions.answer: Sandals and towels are essential gear for a trip to the beach.
questions.explanation: Compound subjects joined by 'and' require a plural verb.

questions.question: Choose the sentence in which the subject and verb agree.
options: The president or the vice president are speaking today.
The president or the vice president is speaking today.
questions.answer: The president or the vice president is speaking today.
questions.explanation: Two singular subjects connected by 'or' require a singular verb.

questions.question: Choose the sentence in which the subject and verb agree.
options: Either Cassie or Marie pays the employees this afternoon.
Either Cassie or Marie pay the employees this afternoon.
questions.answer: Either Cassie or Marie pays the employees this afternoon.
questions.explanation: Singular subjects joined by 'either...or' take a singular verb.
The fixed phrase 'Time and tide' takes the singular verb 'waits'.

questions.sentence: The state of his affairs ________ sure to cause anxiety to his creditors.
questions.explanation: The head noun 'state' is singular, so 'was' is required.
The compound subject 'My father and I' takes a plural verb.

questions.sentence: He or his friends ________ responsible for this.
questions.explanation: With 'or', the verb agrees with the closer subject 'friends' (plural).

questions.sentence: Neither my friends nor I ________ interested in this offer.
questions.explanation: With 'neither...nor', the verb agrees with the closest subject 'I' ('am').

questions.sentence: Oil as well as gas ________ imported to India.
questions.explanation: The phrase 'as well as gas' does not make the subject plural.

questions.sentence: The mother along with her children ________ waiting in the lobby.
questions.explanation: The subject 'mother' is singular; 'along with her children' is parenthetical.

questions.sentence: Many a man ________ lost his life at sea.
questions.explanation: The expression 'Many a [noun]' always takes a singular verb.

questions.sentence: The Pickwick Papers ________ written by Charles Dickens.
questions.explanation: Book titles take singular verbs even if they end in 's'.

questions.sentence: More than 10,000 kilometers ________ India from Europe.
questions.explanation: Distances are treated as a single unit/amount and take singular verbs.

questions.question: Choose the sentence in which the subject and verb agree.
options: Neither the doctor nor the nurses were able to explain the patient's sudden recovery.
Neither the doctor nor the nurses was able to explain the patient's sudden recovery.
questions.answer: Neither the doctor nor the nurses were able to explain the patient's sudden recovery.
questions.explanation: With 'neither...nor', the verb agrees with the subject closest to it. 'Nurses' is plural, so 'were' is correct.

questions.question: Choose the sentence in which the subject and verb agree.
options: A majority of the committee members is in favor of the proposal.
A majority of the committee members are in favor of the proposal.
questions.answer: A majority of the committee members are in favor of the proposal.
questions.explanation: When 'a majority of' is followed by a plural countable noun ('members'), it takes a plural verb ('are').

questions.question: Choose the sentence in which the subject and verb agree.
options: The committee meets every Thursday to discuss community affairs.
The committee meet every Thursday to discuss community affairs.
questions.answer: The committee meets every Thursday to discuss community affairs.
questions.explanation: Collective nouns like 'committee' take singular verbs when the group acts as a single unified entity.

questions.question: Choose the sentence in which the subject and verb agree.
options: Three-fourths of the cake was eaten before the party even started.
Three-fourths of the cake were eaten before the party even started.
questions.answer: Three-fourths of the cake was eaten before the party even started.
questions.explanation: Fractions take a singular verb when referring to a singular noun or uncountable quantity ('cake').

questions.question: Choose the sentence in which the subject and verb agree.
options: There is a set of keys and a wallet on the kitchen table.
There are a set of keys and a wallet on the kitchen table.
questions.answer: There is a set of keys and a wallet on the kitchen table.
questions.explanation: The primary subject following 'there is' is 'a set' (singular collective unit), making 'is' correct.

questions.question: Choose the sentence in which the subject and verb agree.
options: Not only the director but also the actors was praised after the premiere.
Not only the director but also the actors were praised after the premiere.
questions.answer: Not only the director but also the actors were praised after the premiere.
questions.explanation: With correlative conjunctions like 'not only...but also', the verb agrees with the closer subject ('actors' -> 'were').

questions.question: Choose the sentence in which the subject and verb agree.
options: Politics is a subject that generates intense debate among scholars.
Politics are a subject that generates intense debate among scholars.
questions.answer: Politics is a subject that generates intense debate among scholars.
questions.explanation: Nouns ending in '-ics' representing fields of study or single concepts (like 'politics' or 'mathematics') take singular verbs.

questions.question: Choose the sentence in which the subject and verb agree.
options: One of my best friends who lives in Chicago is visiting this weekend.
One of my best friends who live in Chicago is visiting this weekend.
questions.answer: One of my best friends who live in Chicago is visiting this weekend.
questions.explanation: In relative clauses preceded by 'one of those [plural noun] who', the verb in the relative clause agrees with the plural noun ('friends who live'). The main sentence verb then agrees with 'one' ('is visiting').

questions.question: Choose the sentence in which the subject and verb agree.
options: Ten miles is a long distance to run without proper preparation.
Ten miles are a long distance to run without proper preparation.
questions.answer: Ten miles is a long distance to run without proper preparation.
questions.explanation: Expressions of specific measurement, distance, time, or monetary amounts function as a single unit and take a singular verb.

questions.question: Choose the sentence in which the subject and verb agree.
options: The team members, as well as the head coach, are celebrating their championship victory.
The team members, as well as the head coach, is celebrating their championship victory.
questions.answer: The team members, as well as the head coach, are celebrating their championship victory.
questions.explanation: Phrases starting with 'as well as' do not alter the main subject. The main subject 'team members' is plural, requiring 'are'.
